Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) The Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Program is requesting that undergraduate students be able to declare a minor on Interdisciplinary Neuroscience by completing a minimum of 18 credits from the major.
Students must complete an application for the minor that is approved and signed by the INP coordinator and the INP Director.
Application for the INP minor must be filed in the INP Director’s office no later than the beginning of the student’s final semester or term but may be submitted as early as the first semester of the junior year.
Filing for a minor earlier than the junior year is subject to approval by the student’s degree-granting college.
A minimum grade point average of 2.00 must be earned in the minor courses, and a minimum of 12 of the 18 credits must be at the 200 level or above.
At least eight of the credits required for the minor must be earned at the University of Rhode Island.
Courses used to fulfill general education requirements may also be used for the minor.

Up to two courses required in a major program may be used to apply to both the major and minor fields of study (i.e., students may not obtain a minor if their major is interdisciplinary neuroscience).
Students may not take courses required for the minor on a pass-fail basis.
The requirements for the minor must be completed prior to graduation.
Successful completion of the Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Minor will be reflected on the student’s official transcript upon graduation.
Graduates who have earned an undergraduate degree with a minor from URI and who are then readmitted to the university to pursue an alternate major or degree, may apply for that purpose all credits earned in pursuit of the previous minor field of study.
The specific course requirements for the Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Minor include the following: • NEU 101: Foundations of Neuroscience 3 credits • NEU 110: Neuroscience Seminar 1 credit • NEU 210: Neuroethics and Diversity 3 credits • NEU 230: Neuroscience Professional Development 1 credit • NEU 262: Neuroscience Research Methods 4 credits • NEU 301: Cellular & Molecular Neuroscience 3 credits • NEU 310: Developmental OR NEU 320: Clinical 3 credits

Change to Adult Education Master’s program A Notice of Change form was submitted in fall of 2021 and approved in January of 2021 to move the program to the online accelerated calendar (URIOnline). The intended date of change was September of 2021. During the process of transition, we determined that implementing the changes would be problematic. In particular, only students who are registered in URIOnline programs can take courses in URIOnline courses. The issues are as follows: • Currently, we have a contract with the Navy and students in the ETMS specialization are required to take 2 courses outside of the School of Education (MBA courses, in particular) to meet the needs of their program. We tried to find substitutions, but these were not acceptable to the Navy. • Students in the joint PhD in Education Program at URI/RIC who choose the Adult Education specialization are required to take some of their specialization courses in the Adult Education Master’s program. • Students in the TESOL, MBA, and other programs take our courses as electives in the summer. • Students in other education specializations take two courses housed in AE (EDC 529 and EDC 575). Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) in multiple fields toward an undergraduate degree.

It is well-suited for students whose career goals call for training in more than one discipline or who want a breadth of knowledge in several fields rather than a depth of knowledge in a single discipline.
With this degree, one can be even more directly educated with regard to several, specific, job-relevant studies.
This interdisciplinary “three-minor’ major also may work well for students who do not want to limit their career options by majoring in just one area of study.
For the purposes of this proposal, the word “minor" is used to refer to coursework associated with recognized areas of study (as minors) at the University of Rhode Island.
Specifically, students will complete an application that proposes one thematic or topical concentration made up of three (3) recognized minor areas of study that will not be restricted

to conventional departmental or unit boundaries.
The application must include a statement of rationale for the combination of areas of study.
The application then must be reviewed and approved by the Director of School of Professional and Continuing Studies (or designee).
Students seeking this program must declare it as their major in the same manner, and at the same time,that other URI students declare a major.
It is important to note that, through the completion of this program, students will not receive minors in the three areas of study, rather the integrated coursework will be used to fulfill the requirements of the interdisciplinary major.
Upon completion of the program, the student's approved interdisciplinary concentration will be noted on the university transcript.
Moreover, the Learner Designed major provides an opportunity to develop and pursue a course of study centered on a unifying theme, problem, or issue.
Students earning a degree in Bachelor of Interdisciplinary Studies, Learner Designed major will: · Possess an interdisciplinary perspective by integrating knowledge and skills from three areas of study.

Communicate meaningful connections effectively across disciplinary boundaries.
The Learner Designed major will include: (a) URI General Education Requirements; (b) Minor Area of Study 1 (18- 24 credits), Minor Area of Study 2 (18 -24 credits), and Minor Area of Study 3 (18 -24 credits); (c) BIS 100, 399, ITR 302, 304; and, (d) elective courses totaling 120 credit hours.
The capstone experience (BIS 399) provides a structure that enables the student to integrate knowledge and skills from coursework and related experiences with a research project.
The project must be designed so that it allows the student to demonstrate the integration of subject matter, theory, and practice.
Students are required to meet with the Director of School of Professional & Continuing Studies (or designee) to plan a project proposal.
The Learner Designed major will provide students with a well-rounded education in multiple academic disciplines, allowing them to gain skills employers will find desirable, including critical thinking, communication and creative problem-solving.
Employers appreciate applicants with diverse backgrounds and the ability to integrate multiple viewpoints.
